review_candidates.title: Executive Director - Illinois Partners for Human Service
review_candidates.description: Organizational Overview: Illinois Partners for Human Service Illinois Partners for Human Service (Illinois Partners) is a statewide coalition of health and human service organizations working to create a stronger, more stable, and more equitable human services sector across Illinois. The coalition brings together organizations serving communities throughout the state and works to ensure that Illinoisans have access to the resources and services they need to thrive. Illinois Partners serves as a collective voice for the human services sector, bringing together community-based organizations, advocates, policymakers, researchers, and other stakeholders to advance systemic change. Its work focuses on policy and advocacy, research, training, and communications that strengthen the sector and build broader public understanding of the value of human services. Illinois Partners distinguishes itself by operating without seeking or accepting federal and state grants, allowing the organization to advocate independently for improvements to government funding, contracting, and public policy. The coalition includes approximately 850 health and human service organizations representing every legislative district in Illinois. Partners span a broad range of fields, including behavioral health, early childhood, housing, workforce development, immigration, health care, developmental disabilities, domestic violence prevention, youth services, and services for older adults. Illinois Partners is particularly focused on building collective power across a sector that is often fragmented by geography, issue area, and organizational mission. The organization works to bring diverse voices together around shared priorities, engage policymakers and community leaders, and advocate for public policies and investments that support a sustainable and equitable human services system. Position Summary: Executive Director The Executive Director joins Illinois Partners for Human Service at an important moment of momentum and opportunity. With a statewide network of approximately 850 coalition partners, a growing presence in policy and advocacy, and a clear opportunity to strengthen the human services sector’s collective voice, Illinois Partners is positioned to expand its influence and impact across the state. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director will serve as the organization’s chief executive, public representative, coalition builder, and senior advocate. The ED will work closely with the Board, staff, coalition partners, policymakers, funders, and community leaders to advance Illinois Partners’ mission and strengthen the organization’s role as a leading voice for health and human services in Illinois. This is a highly external and relationship-driven leadership role. The Executive Director will build and mobilize relationships across the state, engage directly with legislators and government leaders, represent the sector in policy conversations, and help partners understand the power of working collectively. The successful candidate will bring a deep understanding of policy and advocacy, an organizing mindset, and the ability to translate complex issues into a compelling case for action. The Executive Director will serve as a vital strategic partner to the Board of Directors, working intentionally and collaboratively to establish organizational priorities, allocation of resources, and navigate the complexity and nuance of the shifting state legislative and regulatory environment. Financially, the Executive Director will inherit an organization operating a budget of $700,000, and a staff of 5, including 3 full-time team members, and 2 part-time employees. Illinois Partners is primarily funded through voluntary coalition partner contributions and foundational support through granting opportunities, with a small percentage of revenue generated by individual donations. Illinois Partners does not seek or accept funding from government entities. As a result, the next leader will have experience forging and stewarding relationships with partner organizations and institutional funders to expand and diversify revenue. The next Executive Director will lead Illinois Partners through its next phase of organizational development. This leader will continue to shape and advance policy work like the Living Wages, Thriving Communities campaign, and will be integral in bringing partners together around shared priorities that help move this work forward on behalf of the entire state. The organization has a strong foundation and an engaged coalition, but there is an opportunity to identify a focused set of initiatives where Illinois Partners can lead, strengthen partner engagement, expand its team and infrastructure, and build the financial resources needed to sustain and grow its work. This leader will bring clarity, courage, and conviction while maintaining the collaborative spirit that defines Illinois Partners. Key responsibilities include: Serve as the chief executive and public face of Illinois Partners, providing clear strategic direction and representing the organization and its coalition of partners with policymakers, funders, civic leaders, community organizations, and other stakeholders, while setting a thoughtful, data-driven agenda to maximize the organization’s advocacy impact . Engage and mobilize a powerful statewide coalition, strengthening relationships among Illinois Partners’ approximately 850 partner organizations and creating meaningful opportunities for partners to shape priorities, participate in advocacy, and act collectively. Lead policy and advocacy efforts in Springfield and throughout Illinois, serving as a registered lobbyist and developing relationships with legislators, state agencies, elected officials, and other decision-makers to advance policies that strengthen the human services sector. Fundraise to strengthen the organization’s financial sustainability, working with the Board, staff, and funders to increase foundation support, deepen partner contributions, develop multi-year commitments, and build toward a sustainable annual operating model. Identify a focused set of strategic initiatives where Illinois Partners can lead and make a meaningful difference, balancing the breadth of the coalition with clear priorities and disciplined execution. Develop and communicate a compelling vision for the future of Illinois’ human services sector, helping policymakers, funders, partners, and the broader public understand the value of human services and the importance of sustained investment. Serve as a trusted advocate and thought partner to coalition members, helping organizations navigate policy challenges, connect with decision-makers, and use their collective voice more effectively. Strengthen Illinois Partners’ capacity as a statewide organizing and advocacy organization, building systems and strategies that allow the coalition to mobilize partners quickly around emerging opportunities and threats. Lead organizational strategy and implementation, including the next phase of strategic planning, ensuring that the organization’s goals, resources, staffing, partnerships, and activities are aligned around a clear set of priorities. Lead and develop a high-performing team, providing clarity around roles and expectations while expanding organizational capacity in policy, advocacy, communications, partner engagement, and operations as resources allow. Elevate Illinois Partners’ visibility and voice, using research, communications, public speaking, media, convenings, and strategic partnerships to increase recognition of the organization and the broader human services sector. Leadership Competencies & Personal Characteristics Coalition Leadership & Organizing The Executive Director will be an accomplished coalition builder who knows how to bring diverse organizations and perspectives together around shared priorities. They will understand that Illinois Partners’ influence comes from the breadth and engagement of its network and will bring an organizing mindset to mobilizing partners, empowering member organizations, and building collective power across the state. Policy, Advocacy & Government Relations The successful candidate will bring meaningful experience in public policy and advocacy, with the credibility and relationships necessary to operate effectively. The Executive Director must have a strong understanding of the unique challenges of the political and legislative landscape in Springfield and across the state of Illinois. They will understand how policy is developed, how coalitions influence decision-makers, and how to translate the priorities of a diverse sector into a clear and compelling advocacy agenda. Experience as a lobbyist or registered lobbyist is not required but is strongly valued. Fundraising and Strategic Growth Illinois Partners is seeking a leader who can see beyond the organization’s current structure and identify where it can have greater impact. The Executive Director will bring vision and ambition while remaining grounded in the realities of leading a small organization and a complex coalition. This leader will partner with the Board and staff to identify opportunities for new revenue generation and fund development, while maintaining strong relationships with current funders to grow and diversify the existing portfolio of foundation support, partner contributions, and individual giving. The next leader should have a proven track record of stewarding these relationships, using data-informed insights to expand fundraising infrastructure and support consistent donor cultivation. Relationship Building & Communication The Executive Director will be an engaging and authentic communicator who builds trust quickly and can connect with people across sectors, geographies, and organizational roles. They will be comfortable speaking with legislators, nonprofit leaders, funders, community members, and frontline workers and will be able to communicate complex policy issues in clear, accessible language. Leadership Rooted in Equity Illinois Partners serves as a collective voice for the human services sector, collaborating with non-profit organizations that work directly in equity-sensitive spaces on issues including, but not limited to immigration, domestic violence, and disability services. The next ED will lead with an equity-centered approach to operations, communication, and collaboration. They will have familiarity and respect for the nuanced work of coalition partners and highlight the experiences and real-world policy impacts affecting historically marginalized communities. Location, Compensation and Benefits This position is based in Illinois, with an office space available in Chicago. Illinois Partners offers a hybrid work environment with flexibility to work from different parts of the state; however, the Executive Director is expected to be in the office as required to conduct meetings, team activities, and administrative duties, with additional in-person engagement required for partner events, advocacy activities, and other organizational commitments. The role requires significant travel to Springfield, particularly during the Illinois legislative session from January through May. The Executive Director can expect to be in Springfield approximately two to four times per month during session, generally Tuesday through Thursday, in addition to travel throughout Illinois for coalition and partner engagement. The salary range for this position is $130,000 to $160,000, commensurate with experience, and includes a competitive benefits package. How to Express Interest To express your interest in this opportunity, please submit your resume and cover letter on Maneva Group's website . All inquiries and discussions will be handled with the utmost confidentiality. This position is available immediately, and applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the role is filled. About Maneva Group Maneva Group is a leading woman- and minority-owned executive search firm dedicated to connecting exceptional talent with organizations committed to making a meaningful impact. Through a consultative and client-focused approach, Maneva Group partners with mission-driven organizations to build transformative leadership teams. Our name, Maneva, comes from the combination of two Sanskrit words: “ Mānav ” meaning mankind & “ Sevā ” meaning service. We are driven by the ideal of our name - service to humanity.

review_candidates.title: Editorial Director
review_candidates.description: The International News Media Association (INMA) is the global association for the news media industry — broadcasters, newspapers, magazines, and digital natives on six continents — and its editorial output is the connective tissue of the membership: daily blogs, eight-plus strategic reports a year, newsletters, and the Web site through which members experience all of it. We are looking for an Editorial Director to own that output end to end: its volume, its quality, its regularity, and its intellectual standing. This is a senior role. You will own the content calendar. You will be generating a pipeline of content from a membership of thousands of practitioners who have things to say and rarely get asked. You will embrace AI and understand its intricacies – what to double down on, what to avoid. You are part editor, part content recruiter, part product owner. INMA is small (15+ FTEs plus contractors) but mighty. While the editorial team is small, we occasionally feel like a newsroom on deadline. Speed and accuracy are crucial. What you will own Blog volume and the member pipeline. INMA currently publishes around three blog posts a day. The target is five or more, and the growth comes chiefly from members at media companies rather than paid contractors. That means building and working a bench of member contributors — spotting the executive who gave a strong conference talk, the practitioner who posted something sharp on LinkedIn, the case study buried in a report — and turning them into regular voices. Recruiting, briefing, chasing, editing and encouraging is the daily work of this role. We want every corporate member per year to be a contributor. The editing process. Every piece that carries the INMA name reads cleanly, argues clearly and is factually sound. You set and run the editorial standard for a stable of contract writers and Initiative Leads, from commissioning through publication, including headlines, imagery, and presentation on the site. Style and standards. You know the Associated Press Stylebook cold — not as a reference you consult but as a reflex — and you understand that INMA bends it. Our house style is AP at its spine with an international, typically British, overlay: spellings, dates, currencies, titles, place names and the vocabulary of a global industry rather than an American one (you love the Oxford comma and Economist-like style). You will be the guardian of that style, the person who codifies it where it is currently tribal knowledge, and the one who applies it consistently across contract writers, member contributors and Initiative Leads who each arrive with their own habits. Consistency across at least five posts a day, eight reports a year and every newsletter is the job, and the reader should never be able to tell which of a dozen hands touched a piece. Strategic reports. Eight or more a year, delivered on a published schedule rather than when they happen to be finished. You will manage the calendar with the Initiative Leads and outside authors, edit substantively as well as for style, and see each report through design and launch, including how it is promoted to members. Products. The Daily Member Update, the weekly newsletters, initiative newsletters, The Distillation, and the editorial architecture of INMA.org are yours. Ownership means their format, their voice, their metrics and their evolution — not only filling the slots. Working with AI. INMA uses AI as an editorial instrument, not a replacement for editorial judgment. We produce complex distillations — of conferences, study tours, master classes and hundreds of hours of transcripts — that would be impossible at human speed alone, and we expect this to grow. You will direct that work: framing the questions, shaping the outputs, checking them against what was actually said and done, and applying the same editorial standard to a machine-assisted synthesis as to a human-written blog. At the same time, the core of INMA’s editorial remains human-contributed — members and Initiative Leads writing from experience — and part of your job is to keep the line between the two clear to readers and to yourself. You should arrive already fluent in these tools and curious about what they will do next; you should also arrive with a sceptic’s eye for where they fail. Intellectual partnership. INMA’s Initiative Leads are among the most respected thinkers in their fields. You need to be a peer to them: able to challenge a thesis, sharpen an argument, spot the story inside a data set, and bring your own view of where the industry is heading. This is the difference between an editor and an Editorial Director. Who you are You have led an editorial operation — a newsroom desk, a trade publication, a B2B content function, or a think-tank’s publishing arm — and have the scars to show for hitting daily deadlines and long-form ones at the same time. You know the news media business from the inside: subscriptions, advertising, product, newsroom transformation, the platform relationships, and the AI transition. You edit with a light hand and a sharp eye, and you can make an executive who “doesn’t write” produce 800 good words. You have a thorough knowledge of the international news media markets. This isn't designed for ramp-up ... we are seeking someone who can come in a tell us more about the global media market than we know. You are fluent in AP style and equally at home in British and international usage — the rare editor who can move between the two without hesitation. That profile is most often found at an international wire service, a global trade title, or a U.S. organisation writing for a worldwide audience, and candidates should expect an editing test that checks for both sides of it. You are an active, hands-on user of AI in editorial work — prompting, evaluating and editing machine-assisted synthesis — and you can articulate where it belongs in a publishing workflow and where it does not. You are organised enough to run a 12-month reports calendar and relaxed enough to run it across a dozen time zones. You are comfortable in a small, distributed team where you will do the work as well as direct it. Nice to have: experience with e-mail platforms and CMS administration, familiarity with analytics tooling, and a second language. How the role works Remote, reporting to the Executive Director and CEO, working daily with Initiative Leads and the marketing and production team. Occasional travel to INMA events. This is a full-time position with a pay range of US$105K to US$120K per year plus health/life and 401(k). Measures of success in year one Blog output sustained at five-plus posts a day with a growing share from members; every scheduled report published in its scheduled month; a codified INMA style guide in use by every contributor; measurable improvement in newsletter engagement; and Initiative Leads who describe you as making their work better.

Quản lý đơn giá vật tư/thiết bị các công trình xây dựng dân dụng, hạ tầng kỹ thuật. Lập tổng mức đầu tư theo suất vốn đầu tư xây dựng các loại hình công trình. Quản lý và kiểm soát chi phí ngân sách xây dựng trong quá trình triển khai dự án. Thường xuyên cập nhật các tiêu chuẩn, quy định của Nhà nước, các thay đổi về chế độ chính sách liên quan đến chi phí dầu tư xây dựng. Kiến thức chuyên môn: Trình độ học vấn: Đại học chuyên ngành xây dựng/ kinh tế xây dựng/ giao thông... Có kiến thức sâu rộng về xây dựng, kết cấu công trình, trình tự và biện pháp thi công xây dựng, đơn giá, định mức, sử dụng thành thạo phần mềm dự toán. Hiểu biết, có kiến thức về đầu tư dự án, về thủ tục, hồ sơ dự án, pháp lý trong lĩnh vực đầu tư xây dựng. Kỹ năng công việc: Kỹ năng phân tích, tổng hợp, lập kế hoạch, viết tốt. Làm việc độc lập và làm việc nhóm tốt. Kỹ năng, kinh nghiệm làm việc với các cơ quan chức năng và đối tác trong thực hiện dự án (tư vấn, nhà thầu, nhà cung cấp,...). Xử lý công việc nhanh và hiệu quả. Kinh nghiệm tối thiểu: 03 năm làm chuyên môn trong lĩnh vực tương đương.

review_candidates.title: Chief of Staff
review_candidates.description: Mō Te Puni Kōkiri | About Te Puni Kōkiri Te Puni Kōkiri is the Government’s principal policy advisor on Māori wellbeing and iwi and Māori relationships with the Crown whilst working to advance the aspirations of whānau, hapū, iwi and Māori. Guided by our vision of Thriving Whānau - recognising that when whānau thrive, so too do communities, hapū, iwi and Aotearoa - this is an exciting time to join Te Puni Kōkiri and help shape the Ministry’s future influence, impact and contribution to outcomes for Māori. Mō te tūranga | About the role Reporting directly to the Secretary for Māori Development, you will act as a key conduit between Te Puni Kōkiri, the Minister for Māori Development, Ministers' offices, central agencies and senior public sector leaders, helping ensure Te Puni Kōkiri is well positioned to deliver its priorities and maximise its impact for whānau, hapū, iwi and Māori. The Chief of Staff will often represent the Secretary in meetings, discussions and engagements, carrying their authority, trust and confidence and helping advance the agency’s priorities and strategic objectives. This includes engaging with Ministers, senior public sector leaders, Māori leaders and other key stakeholders on the Secretary's behalf when required. Success requires someone with the judgement, integrity and political acuity to know when to act, when to challenge, and when to escalate. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, you will help connect people, priorities and information across the organisation, coordinate responses to complex and sensitive issues, and ensure critical decisions are translated into action. Key Aspects Of The Role Include Acting as a trusted adviser and sounding board to the Secretary for Māori Development. Providing strategic advice on complex organisational, political and system issues. Supporting and enhancing the effectiveness of the Executive Leadership Team. Leading and coordinating cross-organisational priorities and sensitive issues. Supporting the Secretary’s relationships and influence across government and Māori settings. Contributing to the stewardship, performance and future direction of Te Puni Kōkiri. Mōu | About you You will be a seasoned public sector leader, with the credibility and confidence to operate effectively in complex, high-trust environments. With a deep understanding of the machinery of government and the political landscape, you will have a proven track record advising Chief Executives, Ministers and senior decision-makers. You will bring credibility with Māori leaders, iwi, Māori organisations and communities, underpinned by a deep understanding of the opportunities and challenges shaping Māori social, economic and cultural development. Grounded in te Ao Māori, you will build trusted relationships and operate confidently across both government and Māori settings. As The Successful Candidate, You Will Bring Significant senior leadership experience within the public sector or a similarly complex environment. Deep knowledge of the machinery of government and the political operating environment. Outstanding strategic thinking and analytical capability. Exceptional relationship management, communication and stakeholder engagement skills. Strong understanding of Te Tiriti o Waitangi and confidence operating within Te Ao Māori and tikanga Māori environments. The confidence to challenge thinking, test assumptions and provide robust advice, while maintaining trusted relationships and collective ownership of decisions. A reputation for integrity, discretion and sound judgement. Me pēhea te tono | To apply To request an information pack, or for a confidential discussion regarding the role, please contact: Carl Church, Kaiwhakahaere Matua | Managing Director, Niche Recruitment 021 166 6441 | carl.church@nicherecruitment.co.nz Moana Temel, Kaiwhakahaere | Director, Niche Recruitment 021 499 902 | moana.temel@nicherecruitment.co.nz Applications close at 9am Monday 2 November 2026.
